subject: Clarify mid-cycle embed replay / apportionment on March invoice
messages:
From: Morgan Blake <morgan@vectory.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinOps Team <finops@vectory.com>
Date: 2028-03-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle embed surge on March invoice

Hi Aisha,

We spotted a pretty significant embed usage spike on our March invoice (see attached vectory_invoice_Mar2028.pdf) — total embed units between 2028-03-15 00:00 UTC and 2028-03-16 12:00 UTC are ~3x our normal baseline. We haven't changed anything on our side (no new batch jobs scheduled).

Two quick questions:
- Can Redwood provide a per-route/per-key breakdown for that window (we use a mix of realtime API and a nightly async ingest pipeline)?
- Is it possible we were charged for an embed replay/backfill or duplicate requests? If so, can you propose a provisional credit while you investigate?

I've attached the invoice and our FinOps contact (finops@vectory.com). If you need sample request IDs from our side I can pull those.

Thanks — this one is blocking our close of month reconciliation.

Morgan Blake
Head of FinOps, Vectory Analytics
Morgan Blake | morgan@vectory.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: vectory_invoice_Mar2028.pdf
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Blake <morgan@vectory.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-19T10:03:45-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle embed surge on March invoice

Hi Morgan — thanks for flagging this and apologies for the disruption. Looping in Neha from Billing so we can get a quick breakdown.

Quick note on what we'll do immediately:
- Billing will pull per-route, per-api-key usage for 2028-03-14 through 2028-03-18 and look for replay/duplicate patterns.
- Engineering will scan ingest telemetry for backfill/retry bursts tied to your project id (please send any sample request ids you can).

I'm attaching a small CSV stub (usage-sample-ids.csv) — if you can return with 3-5 request IDs from the spike window that will speed up root cause. Neha, can you confirm whether we have any open router windowing incidents around the 15th?

I'll follow up as soon as we have counts.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha@redwood.ai

Attachments: usage-sample-ids.csv
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Blake <morgan@vectory.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-19T15:22:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle embed surge on March invoice — preliminary findings

Hi Morgan / Aisha — I pulled telemetry and have a preliminary breakdown. TL;DR: we found an overlap between async ingest retries and realtime prefetch behavior that caused duplicate embed write-attribution for a subset of your keys during 2028-03-15 02:40 UTC — 2028-03-16 11:05 UTC.

What we observed (summary):
- Your account uses both the async-batch Ingest route (route_id: ingest-batch-7f) and the realtime/embed endpoint (route_id: embed-realtime-2).
- On 2028-03-15 at ~02:40 UTC a scheduled backfill job retried a window that had partially completed earlier; concurrently, the realtime prefetch flag caused some requests to be materialized and counted twice when the router re-tried batches.
- Affected request count (preliminary): 42,860 embed units double-counted. Normal baseline for that window: ~14,200 units.

Proposed remedial action:
1) We will apply a pro-rata credit to cover the double-counted units. Proposed credit: USD 1,564.50 (calculated from your plan rate for embed units).
2) We'll adjust the March invoice line item and issue a corrected invoice + credit memo within 5 business days once you confirm.
3) Engineering will deploy a deterministic de-duplication filter for mixed-route apportionment that should prevent recurrence; ETA for the filter is two weeks.

Attachments: ingest-telemetry-20280315.zip (contains anonymized request ids, timestamps, and route attributions). Please confirm if you want us to proceed with the proposed credit. If you can share 2-3 of the request ids from your side it will let us pin down the exact retry chain faster.

Notes on next steps and controls:
- If Vectory prefers we can instead issue a provisional credit now (same amount) and finalize after the deep-dive — we do that when customers need immediate close-of-month relief.
- Connor, if you could review for approval on the credit (standard internal threshold applies) that would be great.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Billing Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Morgan Blake <morgan@vectory.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.ai>, FinOps Team <finops@vectory.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T15:04:30-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle embed surge on March invoice — preliminary findings

Thanks Neha — that matches what our logs look like. We pulled a sample of request ids from the 03-15 window and three of them are in the telemetry bundle you attached.

We accept the proposed provisional credit of USD 1,564.50 and would appreciate the corrected invoice + credit memo within 5 business days. Two quick follow-ups:
- Will the de-duplication filter you mentioned apply retroactively to reconcile any edge cases, or only prevent future double-counts?
- Can you confirm the accounting/GL line you will use for the credit memo so our AP team can reconcile quickly?

Aisha — looping you to confirm timing for the final invoice. Connor — please confirm approval to post the provisional credit and update the invoice.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Morgan Blake
Head of FinOps, Vectory Analytics
